messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: New incident created: dns-resolver-nxdomain-spike - paging apac-oncall and network.

emily: noticing spike in 5xxs and client NXDOMAINs from ap-southeast-1 customers starting ~03:14 UTC. Canary shows DNS failures for api.redwood.example.com only from certain resolvers.

jose: can confirm. Our synthetic probes in APAC report a 30% NXDOMAIN rate from one resolver cluster. Other resolvers return healthy A records.

priya: quick health check of endpoints shows backends healthy. This is clearly DNS-level. Any recent GeoDNS config pushes?

marc: no recent pushes from our side in the last 24h. Cloudflare and Route53 both show healthy records. I suspect resolver-side flapping in the provider mesh (CF edge or AWS resolver).

tonya: customers reporting timeouts in-app. CS receiving tickets from two enterprise customers in APAC. We should put a brief "partial outage" note on status while we triage.

ops-bot: Runbook start: GEO_DNS_INVESTIGATION -> collect dig outputs and probe traces.

emily: digging from multiple vantage points:
```
; ap-probe-1
dig +short api.redwood.example.com @203.119.0.1
NXDOMAIN
```
```
; ap-probe-2
dig +short api.redwood.example.com @8.8.8.8
203.0.113.21
```
Some resolvers returning NX, others correct. TTLs are low (60s) but the inconsistency persists.

jose: sending debug headers to client to capture resolver IPs in logs. Also enabling verbose DNS logs on edge for apac proxies.

priya: recommended mitigations: 1) reduce client-side caching TTL if possible, 2) temporarily route apac DNS answers to Route53-only policy (we can flip weights), 3) contact Cloudflare & AWS support with dig traces. My preference: route to provider that shows consistent answers (Route53) while we investigate.

marc: Route53 appears consistent from our probes. We have a prebuilt geo-failover route for APAC -> Route53-primary. I can trigger but needs two approvals per runbook.

ops-bot: geodns.failover_request(APAC->Route53) created. Requires 2 approvers.

emily: approve.

priya: approve. Triggering failover in 20s.

emily: posting status: "Investigating DNS failures impacting some APAC customers. Mitigation in progress."

marc: applying failover: setting GeoPolicy APAC = Route53-only, TTL->30.

ops-bot: action queued: geodns.apply(policy=APAC:Route53, ttl=30) by marc -- applied.

emily: forcing re-resolve on APAC edges:
```bash
# call edge admin to flush host cache
for host in edge-1 edge-2 edge-3; do
  curl -s -XPOST https://$host.internal/_flushdns -H "Authorization: Bearer ***" -d '{"host":"api.redwood.example.com"}'
done
```
Flushed 3/3.

jose: probes now show consistent Route53 answers from APAC vantage points. NXDOMAIN rate dropping in canaries.

cs-bot: Notifying impacted customers: templated message queued to send to affected enterprise customers; CS owner: tonya.

priya: opened tickets with providers: Cloudflare ticket CF-24680 and AWS SR-72654321 with sample traces and timestamps.

marc: Cloudflare support replied: "we observed a brief routing loop in edge resolvers causing intermittent NX responses for some authoritative responses ~03:10-03:18 UTC. Engineering roll performed. Asking for customer dig logs."

jose: AWS responded: "no anomalies observed on Route53. Suggest customers use health-check-based failover if using mixed providers."

emily: monitoring metrics: canary error rate fell from 30% -> 1.8% within 2 minutes after failover. Production error delta also falling.

tonya: CS outbound: sent mitigation note + ETA for update. Affected customers offered temporary SLA credit if they need it.

ops-bot: Severity updated to Sev2. Pager escalation throttled.

priya: plan for revert: keep Route53-only for 30m while we watch for recurrence. After 30m of stable probes, revert to balanced weighting and raise TTL to normal.

emily: agree. Also let's add an automation item: if resolver-answer divergence > 20% for 5m, auto-trigger geodns failover to the most consistent provider (requires manual confirmation currently).

marc: capturing action items: (1) postmortem owner = marc, (2) automation ticket for auto-failover draft, (3) runbook update to include provider-side resolver flapping checklist, (4) CS follow-ups with affected customers.

jose: Cloudflare sent a follow-up: "issue mitigated on our side; we recommend customers that use both providers to staggering TTL changes when switching providers to avoid transient divergence."

priya: starting 30m stability timer. Keeping TTL=30.

45m later...

emily: stability window complete. No NXDOMAINs reported in probes. Preparing controlled revert to balanced weights.

marc: reverting GeoPolicy APAC -> balanced (Route53=50, Cloudflare=50), TTL back to 60. Applying now.

ops-bot: geodns.apply(policy=APAC:balanced, ttl=60) by marc -- applied.

jose: flushed edge caches again. All probes return balanced answers. No spike in errors.

emily: posting status update: "Service restored for all customers. Root cause: transient Cloudflare edge resolver routing loop causing intermittent NXDOMAINs. Mitigation: temporarily routed APAC to Route53; postmortem to follow."

tonya: CS follow-up sent to customers with timeline and mitigation details.

marc: closing incident channel in 10m; collecting logs for RCA. Postmortem ticket created: PM-9834.

ops-bot: Incident resolved flag set to monitoring -> resolved pending RCA.

emily: notes for postmortem: quantify impacted requests (~12k failed DNS lookups), duration ~8-12 minutes of peak impact, recommend auto-detection thresholds and runbook improvements.

priya: will own draft RCA and automation spec.

incident-bot: incident closed in 1h 2m. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
